note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Several days of acute diarrhea with abdominal cramping, associated nausea and vomiting. Diarrhea described as very watery and frequent; stools loose with no reported blood. Feels hot/febrile though no temperature taken.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms started about 3 days ago (around Monday/Tuesday); diarrheal episodes occurring nearly hourly while awake; currently multiple episodes per day with ongoing symptoms.
- Pain: Crampy abdominal pain, midline lower abdomen, intermittent, rated about 6/10 at worst.
- Nausea/vomiting: Yes, present; one episode of vomiting after milk; vomiting described as less prominent than diarrhea.
- Hydration/urine: Drinking water, but urine output described as decreased/fewer voids.
- Diet: Last solid intake was lunch today; meals may be poorly tolerated; fluids pass through quickly.
- Fever: Feels hot; no measured fever provided.
- Past medical history: Generally fit and well; no chronic illnesses noted.
- Medications: Occasional paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); no regular medications.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives with sister and mother; works in an office in Central London (government role); smokes socially; occasional alcohol use.
- Family history: Father has colon cancer (diagnosed; currently described as in third stage); details uncertain.
- Additional notes: Brother has had similar symptoms for several days; no clear triggering food identified.

Objective:
- No vital signs or physical examination findings documented in transcript.
- Symptoms reported by patient:
  - Watery diarrhea: very frequent, nearly hourly when awake.
  - Abdominal pain: midline lower abdomen, intermittent, level of distress about 6/10.
  - Nausea/vomiting: present (one milk-related episode).
  - Fever: patient reports feeling hot; no measured temperature available.
  - Urine: decreased frequency noted.
  - Blood in stool: not reported.
  - Food intake: lunch consumed today with loose stools afterward.
- No objective lab tests or imaging results provided.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Gastroenteritis (likely viral)
   - Assessment: Symptoms consistent with gastroenteritis as described by patient and clinician.
   - Differential diagnoses: viral gastroenteritis; bacterial gastroenteritis; food poisoning; inflammatory bowel disease less likely given acute onset and symptom pattern.
   - Investigations planned: none at this time; advise monitoring for dehydration or red-flag symptoms.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Oral rehydration: Diarolyte (over-the-counter) recommended to replace fluids/electrolytes.
     - Hydration: encourage clear fluids initially; avoid alcohol.
     - Diet: clear fluids first; advance to soft diet (soup, mashed foods) as tolerated.
     - Medications: continue paracetamol as needed for fever/pain; dose/frequency not documented; avoid antidepressants or other meds not indicated.
     - Red flags and follow-up: if symptoms do not settle within 48 hours or if signs of dehydration develop, patient should contact the clinic.
   - Referrals: none.

Quality checks (document quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate) and weight not provided.
  - Complete medication reconciliation (dosage, route, frequency for paracetamol not documented).
  - Physical examination findings (abdominal exam, signs of dehydration) not documented.
  - Objective data (laboratory tests or stool studies) not obtained.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Dialogue was generally clear; some repetition and informal phrasing, but actionable clinical information was extractable.
